**From One Pedagogy to Many Classrooms: A Core-and-Contour Strategy for Mandated-Curriculum EdTech** --- ### Executive Summary Exporting a US adaptive-learning platform as a “translated content library” fails in 2026 because education is not entertainment: the state defines the curriculum, parents define trust through cultural proxies, and the procurement channel defines your unit economics. In Vietnam, the product is a high-stakes exam accelerator; in France, it is a teacher-augmentation tool that must respect secular pedagogy and screen-time skepticism; in Saudi Arabia, it is a state-certified digital classroom subject to values compliance and gender-segregated operations; in Kenya, it is a low-bandwidth, portfolio-based companion to the Competency-Based Curriculum (CBC). This strategy adopts a **“Core & Contour”** architecture: - **Invariant Core:** The adaptive engine, knowledge graph, offline-sync infrastructure, and AI tutor backbone are global and fixed-cost. They are **not** pro-rata allocated to emerging-market students; the marginal cost to serve one additional learner is compute at the edge and local content royalties. - **Configurable Pedagogical Model:** The engine is not constructivist by default. It exposes algorithmic parameters—mastery thresholds, spacing intervals, speed-weighting, drilling caps, and teacher-override gates—that are tuned per country so that the *model itself* bends, not merely the content skin. - **Pedagogical Contour:** Curriculum mapping, assessment philosophy, cultural UX, and values moderation are built and governed by **in-country pods with pedagogical veto power** over the central product team. - **Procurement Dualism with Hard Parity Rules:** The same codebase is sold through ministry-level B2G certification (Saudi Arabia, France), direct-to-parent mobile-money subscriptions (Vietnam, Kenya), and low-cost private-school bundles (Kenya). Each channel carries its own CAC and compliance burden, and none subsidizes the other below the **contribution floor**. Feature gating is explicit to prevent channel arbitrage. - **Honest Content Economics:** The platform does not attempt to export US Common Core alignment or American cultural narratives as “neutral” STEM. It maps to mandated national standards and sources local content through publisher partnerships, not central editorial. --- ### 1. Strategic Doctrine: The Three Layers and Hard Trade-Offs | Layer | Function | Global vs. Local | |-------|----------|------------------| | **1. Global Adaptive Core** | Knowledge graph, mastery algorithms, multimodal AI tutor, offline-sync protocol, content-authoring SDK. | **Invariant.** Optimized for low-latency inference and local-edge caching; language-agnostic and curriculum-agnostic at the engine level. | | **2. Country Pedagogical Operating Model** | Curriculum-standard mapping, assessment philosophy, values moderation, language-of-instruction rules, pedagogical UX norms. | **Contour.** Owned by local pods. Vietnam maps to MOET item types; France mirrors *cycles* and *liens avec les programmes*; Saudi integrates religious studies and RTL gender-aware UX; Kenya aligns to CBC competency strands. | | **3. Local Trust & Procurement Interface** | Sales channel, data-residency stack, parental-control framing, payment rails, teacher PD requirements. | **Channel-native.** B2G evidence protocols in Saudi/France; M-Pesa and WhatsApp parent nudges in Kenya; MoMo/ZaloPay weekly packs and tutoring-center B2B in Vietnam. | **Governance Rule:** The central platform guild owns architecture and data schema. The country pod owns pedagogy, content compliance, and algorithmic configuration. **Local PMs have veto power over any feature that violates curriculum alignment or cultural norms.** #### 1.1 How the Core Bends: Algorithmic Trade-Offs The prompt asks for a *balance* between shared technology and local fit. That balance is struck not by changing the engine’s code per country, but by exposing a **Pedagogical Parameter Set** that rewrites the learning path without rewriting the codebase. | Tension | Vietnam | France | |---------|---------|--------| | **Learning science vs. local practice** | Adaptive engines default to spaced repetition and forgetting-curve optimization. Vietnam’s cram culture prizes massed practice and timed mock exams. | Adaptive engines are prescriptive; they decide the next exercise. France’s teacher autonomy is sacred. | | **Resolution** | **“Cram Mode” parameter set:** Massed-practice blocks replace spaced intervals during exam windows; speed-accuracy weighting shifts to 70:30; the engine generates *Mock Exam Sprints* that suppress scaffolding hints and enforce countdown timers. The underlying graph is unchanged; the traversal logic is locally configured. | **“Autonomy Mode” parameter set:** Teachers can lock the learning path to a mandatory sequence, unlock open exploration, or assign printable worksheets that **bypass the algorithm entirely**. The engine becomes a suggestion layer unless the teacher explicitly delegates control. A **repetition cap** prevents drilling beyond three failed attempts, forcing a teacher-facing intervention alert. | | **Product implication** | Students see “Exam Season” tiles, not “Mastery Loops.” Tutors can override the adaptive path with their own weekly test schedule. | Student UI defaults to worksheet export after 15 minutes of screen time. Teacher dashboard is the primary viewport; student gamification is suppressed. | --- ### 2. Country Playbooks: The Four Markets The following markets are treated as distinct product entities. Regional averages are used only for investor narrative, never for curriculum mapping or GTM design. | Dimension | **Vietnam** | **Saudi Arabia** | |-----------|-------------|------------------| | **Curriculum Authority** | MOET. Highly centralized; national textbooks (NXB Giáo dục) are canonical. History and civic education are ideologically sensitive. | Ministry of Education (MoE). Vision 2030–driven; Tatweer funds digital transformation. Islamic Studies, Quranic Arabic, and Naḥw are mandatory. | | **Language of Instruction** | Vietnamese for all core subjects; English taught as foreign language. Platform must be fully Vietnamese, with English modules as a distinct “subject” track. | Arabic (MSA) for core; English growing under Vision 2030. Full RTL; formal honorifics (*ustādh/ustādha*) required for AI tutor personas. | | **Attitude to Foreign Content** | Permitted in STEM, deeply scrutinized in humanities. US-branded platforms face suspicion of cultural dilution; must co-brand with local publishers. | Conservative gatekeeping. Foreign content must pass Sharia-compliance and values review. No LGBTQ+ themes; gender norms strictly mirrored in UX and content. | | **Screen Time / Parental Trust** | Academic screen time is virtuous if linked to exam rank. Parents demand percentile dashboards and comparison to peers. | Permitted if “safe” (*āmin*). Guardian visibility is paramount; family accounts with elder oversight expected. | | **Assessment Culture** | High-stakes, high-frequency. THPT QG (national graduation/university entrance) dominates learning behavior. Drill-and-practice is socially desired. | High-stakes (Qiyas/Tahsili/GAT). Strong rote-memorization culture in religious subjects; adaptive platform must handle both recall and application layers. | | **Algorithmic Posture** | **Cram Mode:** Massed practice, timed gates, speed-weighted scoring, tutor override. | **Mastery Mode with Memorization Layer:** Standard spaced repetition for STEM; audio-loop SRS for Quranic *Tajwīd* and *Fiqh* recall. | | **Primary Procurement** | **B2C / B2B2C.** Parents pay for supplementary “exam weapons.” Tutoring centers (*luyện thi*) are the real gatekeepers. | **B2G / PPP.** Ministry and Tatweer procure at system level; school-by-school deployment. D2C exists but is secondary. | | **Regulatory Red Line** | Cybersecurity law mandates local data storage; content pre-approval for K–12 foreign digital materials. | SDAIA data-sovereignty rules; content moderation board approval; gender-segregated school deployment requirements. | | **Commercial Reality** | Micro-payments via MoMo, ZaloPay, VietQR. Weekly packs aligned with tutoring cash flows. | Per-pupil license fees paid by ministry or insurer-like edu funds. High ASP, 12–24 month sales cycles. Values-moderation staffing and RCT certification are heavy fixed costs that make true D2C viability impossible below a premium niche. | | Dimension | **France** | **Kenya** | |-----------|------------|-----------| | **Curriculum Authority** | Ministère de l’Éducation Nationale. *Programmes* are national; pedagogy is secular (*laïcité*) and centralized through Académies. | KICD (Kenya Institute of Curriculum Development). CBC emphasizes competencies, practical activities, and portfolios over rote exams. | | **Language of Instruction** | French exclusively; English is a subject. Platform must mirror French pedagogical terminology (*CP, CE1, CE2, cycle 2, cycle 3*). | English from Grade 4/5; Swahili and mother tongue in early years. Platform must support multilingual code-switching and audio narration in Swahili. | | **Attitude to Foreign Content** | Hostile to “Silicon Valley” EdTech seen as marketization of public education. Strong preference for *éducation nationale* alignment over “innovation.” | Pragmatic. Foreign content accepted if KICD-approved and affordable. High aspirational demand for digital learning. | | **Screen Time / Parental Trust** | **Digital sobriety.** State bans smartphones in schools; parents and unions deeply skeptical of algorithmic drilling. Platform must justify every minute of screen use. | Mixed. Urban parents accept academic screen time; rural constraints are device/bandwidth, not ideology. CBC portfolio-parent reporting builds trust. | | **Assessment Culture** | Formative emphasis. National exams (*Brevet, Baccalauréat*) exist, but French pedagogy rejects excessive *standardized* drill. Teacher autonomy is sacred. | CBC uses continuous formative assessment (rubrics, projects). KPSEA replaces high-stakes KCPE but retains summative gatekeeping. | | **Algorithmic Posture** | **Autonomy Mode:** Teacher override mandatory; repetition caps; printable worksheet export; reflection prompts before retry. | **CBC Hybrid Mode:** Digital captures knowledge nodes; practical activities captured via offline rubric + photo evidence. Summative prep exists but is visually deprioritized. | | **Device Strategy** | **Dual-track.** School track: tablet-based via Académie RFP, with MDM and classroom cart. Home track: parent-funded browser/Android app on family devices, with strict CNIL consent flows and 1-year data retention. Municipal library device-lending partnerships for equity. | Lightweight Android app; low-resolution video; SMS fallback for progress reports; teacher-facing rubric app on KaiOS or basic smartphone. | | **Primary Procurement** | **B2G/B2B** → Académies / Private schools
**B2C (Niche)** → Paris/urban supplementary | **B2B** → Low-cost private academies
**B2C** → Urban parents (M-Pesa)
**B2G** → Donor-funded tablet programs | | **Regulatory Red Line** | GDPR/CNIL; data must stay in EU. *Laïcité* forbids any religious content or even cultural bias. Accessibility (*RGAA*) mandated. | Data Protection Act 2019; KICD content approval; rural last-mile equity expectations. | | **Commercial Reality** | SaaS per-école or per-Académie. Freemium for individual teachers to bypass procurement friction. Parents rarely pay directly; any D2C price is politically sensitive. | M-Pesa weekly/monthly parent packs; school licenses capped per student; donor-funded tablet deployments (DigiSchool-style). B2B price points are donor-subsidized in pilot phase. | --- ### 3. The Product Architecture: Curriculum, Culture, and Code #### 3.1 The Invariant Core (What Stays Global) The core is **curriculum-agnostic and language-agnostic** by design. It treats learning objectives as abstract nodes in a knowledge graph, leaving the national standard mapping to a configurable overlay. - **Abstract Knowledge Graph:** Decomposes subjects into mastery nodes (e.g., “linear equations,” “photosynthesis,” “past tense”) without attaching them to a national standard at the engine level. - **Adaptive Mastery Engine:** Spaced repetition, forgetting-curve prediction, and difficulty calibration are universal learning-science modules. They operate on learner telemetry, not content provenance. - **Offline-First Sync Protocol:** Critical for Kenya (connectivity gaps) and rural Saudi Arabia. Learner progress syncs asynchronously; content packages download to device edge. - **Multimodal AI Tutor Backbone:** A routing layer that accepts STT/TTS in local accents (Saigon Vietnamese, Hejazi Arabic, Parisian French, Kenyan Swahili/English) and delegates to either global LLMs or locally hosted small models depending on data-sovereignty rules. - **Authoring SDK:** Provided to local publishers (NXB Giáo dục, Obeikan, Hatier, Longhorn) to build lessons that feed into the adaptive engine without central engineering bottlenecks. #### 3.2 The Curriculum Adapter: Standards Mapping as Code Rather than static PDF alignments, each country maintains a **Curriculum Adapter**—a version-controlled API layer that maps national standards to the global knowledge graph. | Market | Adapter Function | Product Implication | |--------|------------------|---------------------| | **Vietnam** | Maps MOET *Chương trình* item types to graph nodes; tags nodes by THPT QG exam frequency (high/medium/low). | Adaptive path prioritizes high-frequency exam item types. “Mock exam” mode simulates national test pacing. | | **Saudi Arabia** | Maps MoE standards including Quranic memorization (*Tajwīd*) and Islamic *Fiqh* strands. | Religious studies are first-class subjects in the adaptive graph, not add-ons. Memorization modules use audio-loop SRS. Gender-specific content pipelines for *Fiqh* where jurisprudence differs. | | **France** | Maps *Programmes* by *cycle* and *domaine*; enforces secular content boundaries. | Teacher dashboard explicitly links each exercise to the official *bulletin officiel*. No gamified “coins”; instead, *validation des compétences*. | | **Kenya** | Maps CBC competency strands and *core values*; integrates practical/project activity nodes. | Parent report prints a CBC-style portfolio, not just a percentile. Tracks learner competencies (communication, creativity) alongside content mastery. Practical activity is captured via hybrid offline-to-digital workflow, not self-reported checkboxes. | #### 3.3 The Cultural-Pedagogical UX Layer | Market | UX Localization | Screen-Time & Parental Framing | |--------|----------------|--------------------------------| | **Vietnam** | Competitive leaderboards by province; “study streaks” celebrated; AI tutor uses informal but respectful *anh/chị/em* pronouns appropriately. | Parent dashboard shows exam readiness score and peer percentile. Screen time is framed as “investment.” | | **Saudi Arabia** | RTL interface; gender-selectable avatars (or explicitly gender-neutral); no music in UX sounds (voice/SFX only); prayer-time quiet modes. | Guardian app with full content visibility and time-lock. “Family learning” mode for sibling co-use respecting gender norms. | | **France** | Minimalist, print-like aesthetic. No flashing rewards or “candy crush” gamification. Teacher-facing UI dominates; student UI is subdued. | Strict daily time caps with enforced breaks. One-click export to printable worksheet to satisfy anti-screen parents/teachers. | | **Kenya** | Lightweight Android app; low-resolution video; SMS fallback for progress reports; Swahili voice UI for early grades. | SMS-based parent nudges in Swahili/English. “CBC Portfolio” printable via local cyber-café.
